benchmarks.name: HUMAN_TP53_SWISSPROT_TOP_HIT
benchmarks.description: Human p53 (TP53) sequence must hit P04637 as top hit against Swiss-Prot with ~100% identity.
benchmarks.ground_truth: P04637 Homo sapiens Tumor suppressor p53 is the canonical Swiss-Prot entry for human p53.
benchmarks.citation: Bairoch A. et al. Nucleic Acids Res. 2005; Matlashewski G. et al. EMBO J. 1984.

benchmarks.name: INSULIN_SWISSPROT_TOP_HIT
benchmarks.description: A BLAST search must return an insulin entry as the top Swiss-Prot hit at ~100% identity.
benchmarks.ground_truth: Insulin B-chain peptide is identical across mammals, so the top Swiss-Prot hit is an insulin entry at ~100% identity regardless of species.

benchmarks.name: HUMAN_TP53_NOT_INSULIN
benchmarks.description: Human p53 must NOT be matched as insulin; top hit must remain p53-family.

benchmarks.name: HUMAN_OXTR_SWISSPROT_TOP_HIT
benchmarks.description: Human oxytocin receptor must hit P30559 as top hit.
benchmarks.ground_truth: P30559 Oxytocin receptor is the human Swiss-Prot entry.

benchmarks.name: HUMAN_HBB_SWISSPROT_TOP_HIT
benchmarks.description: Human beta-globin must hit P68871 as top hit.
benchmarks.ground_truth: P68871 Hemoglobin subunit beta is the human Swiss-Prot entry.
